claude.request:
Today's international headlines:
- US strikes Iran ahead of midterm elections: US officials described the attacks on Qeshm Island as limited and defensive, according to CBS, the BBC's US partner.
- Supreme Court rejects Trump's request to stop California counting disputed votes: The ruling, which comes on the eve of the midterm elections, essentially ends the Trump administration's bid to disqualify the ballots in the state.
- Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says: Officials say at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit a southern Ukrainian village in what the president called an "utterly horrific" attack.
- Thousands of European troops to rehearse Ukraine deployment in event of peace: Western officials stress that any force sent to Ukraine would not take part in any offensive operations.
- Plane may have broken apart ahead of deadly Florida jet crash, say investigators: The National Transportation Safety Board also believes weather could have been a factor in the crash, but warns it is too early to determine the cause.
- Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack: The temperature of freezers in several shops across Europe reportedly rose to as high as 50C.
- Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire: Though unprecedented, the six-day truce has done little to alter the wider trajectory of a war that continues to grinds on.
- Legal challenge to Australia's social media ban to start in High Court: A rights group will argue the world-leading policy robs under-16s of their right to free communication.
- North Korea denies being behind record $6.3bn Binance hack: US government agencies and cyber analysts have blamed Pyongyang for the record-breaking heist.
- Man and boy arrested after allegedly attacking One Nation volunteer with bat: The incident comes amid growing calls for the temperature of political debate in Australia to be turned down.
- Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president: The case, part of the "Farmgate" scandal, has left President Cyril Ramaphosa mired in an impeachment saga.
- Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord: Jos Leijdekkers has been found guilty in absentia of cocaine smuggling and is believed to be in Sierra Leone.

image_provider.prompt: A fractured, pixelated image of a ballot box shattering mid-fall, surrounded by fragments of military ordnance, frozen food packages melting into liquid, and silhouettes of distant marching troops, all rendered in sharp geometric shards against a darkening sky. The composition is split diagonally between order collapsing on one side and cold, systematic chaos on the other. Bold, high-contrast blacks and deep reds dominating. Style: hard-edged digital art with a sense of rapid disintegration.
